blindSummary: A case study in legislative instability: a 2016 law restricted bathrooms to birth-certificate sex and was repealed in 2017 after mass backlash, but a binary-"sex" statute remains. A trans-killings monitoring dataset places this state/province at about 3.0 killings per 100k trans women - a recorded floor - and a July 2026 legal-risk map rates it moderate, alongside two other states/provinces.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (); the underlying legal-reference page surveys state transgender bathroom-access laws and was cited in the dossier for this state/province's post-2016 binary-'sex' statute and for a recorded-killings figure (12 killings, 6.4 per 100k); the latter conflicts with an independent data-journalism outlet's state-by-state chart and is corrected below.

An independent data-journalism essay (16 July 2026): a national data analysis comparing legal-risk categories with trans-killings monitoring records, arguing protective statutes do not predict lower lethal risk for trans women; includes a state rate chart in which this state/province stands at 3.0 killings per 100k trans women with 3+ recorded victims (an acknowledged undercount) and characterises it as moderate-risk.
